Key Performance Indicator Reporting Policy

SCHEDULED successor to the version effective 1 April 2025. Not yet effective; becomes authoritative on 1 September 2026.

KPI	Target (from 1 September 2026)	Reported
Staff turnover	< 20% annualised	Monthly
Training compliance	> 97%	Monthly
Complaints per 100 beds	< 2 per quarter	Quarterly
New: agency usage	< 10% of total hours	Monthly

<!-- freeze-correction-realism-start -->

Indicator ownership

Each approved indicator has a definition, source system, reporting frequency, accountable owner and named reviewer. The definition states inclusions, exclusions, numerator, denominator and treatment of missing data so sites cannot improve a result by changing interpretation. A proposed indicator or target has no reporting authority until the scheduled successor version becomes effective.

Validation and submission

Owners reconcile source totals, investigate material variance and record corrections before submission. Estimates are visibly labelled and replaced when verified data becomes available. Local commentary explains unusual movement without suppressing an adverse result, and access to resident or workforce detail remains limited to people who need it.

Review and action

The governance meeting considers trend, comparison, data quality and whether existing actions are effective. A threshold breach receives an owner and due date rather than being explained away in narrative. Reports, validation evidence, corrections and meeting decisions are retained together, allowing the published position to be reproduced from its source data.

<!-- freeze-correction-realism-end -->

simply because it had not declined; comparing against an external, sector-wide benchmark where available provides a more objective check on whether Alderbridge's own standards remain genuinely ambitious relative to the wider sector, not merely relative to its own past, and helps the Board ask a sharper question than 'are we improving' alone would prompt.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates external benchmarking in practice. The first annual benchmarking exercise finds Alderbridge's medication error rate compares favourably against the available sector-wide data, while its staff training compliance rate sits slightly below the sector median despite appearing strong against Alderbridge's own historical trend; this external comparison prompts a specific investment in training capacity that a purely internal comparison would not have surfaced as a priority.

Frequently asked questions

**Where does the sector-wide data come from?** A relevant industry body or regulator publication, used only where the data is genuinely comparable in methodology and scope to Alderbridge's own measurement. **Does a below-benchmark result mean immediate action is required?** It prompts investigation and, where appropriate, a targeted action plan, following the same structured response as any other quality finding, rather than an automatic, undifferentiated response regardless of the underlying cause.

Training and competency

The Quality Lead receives specific training on identifying a genuinely comparable external dataset and conducting a methodologically sound benchmarking exercise.

Monitoring and compliance

The Board reviews the full quality data set, including the annual external benchmarking result, quarterly, with the full benchmarking report presented once a year.

Record keeping and retention

Audit records, quality indicator data, peer review findings, and the annual external benchmarking report are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This framework was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 May 2023, this version took effect 1 August 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in August 2027.

Communicating quality findings to staff

A quality finding, whether from the central audit, peer review, or the new external benchmarking exercise, is communicated back to the staff at the relevant site in accessible terms, including an honest account of where Alderbridge compares favourably or less favourably against the sector.

Video calls and screen sharing while working remotely

During a video call or screen share involving sensitive information, staff confirm no unauthorised person can view or overhear the call, close any unrelated sensitive document before sharing a screen, and use only Alderbridge-approved conferencing tools rather than a personal account on an unapproved platform, applying the same care to a video meeting as to an in-person conversation about the same information.

Wi-Fi security at an approved home location

Home Wi-Fi used for Alderbridge work is secured with a strong, unique password and up-to-date router firmware, and an entirely open or default-password network is not used for any Alderbridge system; where genuinely uncertain about home network security, IT can advise on basic steps to improve it.

Ending a remote working arrangement

Where a remote working arrangement ends, whether by the employee's own request or a genuine business need, IT confirms the issued device and any remote access credential are returned or revoked promptly, following the same access-removal discipline the IT Acceptable Use Policy sets out for a leaver, since a remote arrangement ending is functionally similar to a change of access requirement even where employment itself continues.

Backing up work created while working remotely

Work saved locally on a remote device, rather than directly to an Alderbridge system, is backed up regularly using the approved method IT provides, since a device fault or loss while working remotely should never result in genuinely lost work, and staff are shown how to confirm their own backup is actually running correctly as part of their remote working setup.

Family members and household members during remote work

A family or household member should never have access to an Alderbridge device or account, even briefly and even for an unrelated purpose such as checking their own personal email, since this creates an unnecessary and entirely avoidable risk to data the household member has no reason to see.

Monitoring and compliance

Record keeping and retention

Approval and review history

This policy was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 6 January 2026 and is scheduled for its next full review on 6 January 2027.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Grievance Procedure and Disciplinary Procedure for how a specific complaint or conduct concern involving discrimination is actually investigated, the Recruitment and Selection Policy and Safer Recruitment Guidance for how equality of opportunity is built into hiring, and the Safeguarding Adults Policy where a dignity concern also meets the safeguarding threshold — these are not duplicated here, since restating them separately would risk the two documents drifting apart at their next independent review.

Extended worked example: a reasonable adjustment for a resident

A worked example illustrates that this policy's dignity commitment applies to people supported, not only staff. A resident at Riverside House living with a visual impairment finds it increasingly difficult to identify her own room among several similar doors on her corridor. Rather than treating this as an inevitable consequence of her condition, staff introduce a simple, high-contrast tactile marker on her door, chosen together with her rather than imposed, and the change is recorded in her care plan as a reasonable adjustment. The registered manager subsequently reviews whether other residents on the same corridor might benefit from a similar approach, rather than treating the adjustment as a one-off fix specific to a single request.

Staff Handbook Full Manual

*Supersedes the version effective 1 September 2024. Adds a consolidated wellbeing and benefits summary section, mirroring the same addition made to the Employee Handbook and Terms document, so a new starter has a single consistent overview of the support and benefits available to them.*

Purpose and scope

This handbook brings together, in one place, the day-to-day information every Alderbridge Care Group employee needs, now including a consolidated wellbeing and benefits summary alongside the flexible working and regional structure information added in the previous version. It applies to every employee at every site.

Welcome and organisational overview

Alderbridge Care Group operates a small number of residential and nursing care homes, each led by its own registered manager, organised into regions each led by a regional manager, supported by organisation-level functions: Human Resources, the Health and Safety Lead, the Safeguarding Lead, and the Chief Executive's office.

Understanding the regional management structure

Each site's registered manager reports to a regional manager, who oversees several sites within a defined geographic area and coordinates activity, such as emergency mutual aid and multi-agency safeguarding support, across those sites.

Employment basics

Every employee receives a written contract setting out their specific role, hours, and pay; this handbook explains the general terms that apply across Alderbridge and points to the specific policy governing a particular topic in more detail.

1. Read this handbook alongside your own contract of employment during induction.
2. Complete all mandatory training assigned to your role within the timescale set by your registered manager.
3. Raise a question about any policy referenced in this handbook with your registered manager or Human Resources.
4. Keep your own personal and emergency contact details up to date with Human Resources.
5. Understand who your own regional manager is and their role, alongside your registered manager's own role.
6. Review the new wellbeing and benefits summary as part of your induction, and revisit it whenever your own circumstances change; this is a new expectation introduced in this version.

Staff Supervision and Appraisal Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Renames the 'Appraisal' section and defined term to
'Annual Performance and Development Review', better reflecting its forward-looking development focus;
the underlying process is unchanged.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group provides regular supervision and an Annual Performance
and Development Review for every member of staff. It applies to every site and every category of
permanent staff.

Policy statement

Regular supervision and a meaningful Annual Performance and Development Review give every staff
member a structured opportunity to reflect on their practice, raise a concern, and plan their own
development, supporting both individual growth and the quality of care residents receive.

Definitions

**Supervision** a regular one-to-one meeting between a staff member and their line manager, focused on
current practice and immediate support needs. **Annual Performance and Development Review** the
renamed term for what the previous version called an appraisal — the annual, more formal review of a
staff member's overall performance over the past year and their development plan for the year ahead.
**Personal development plan** the agreed set of development actions arising from the Annual
Performance and Development Review.

Roles and responsibilities

**Line managers** conduct supervision at least monthly for every direct report and lead the Annual
Performance and Development Review. **HR** monitors that supervision and the Annual Performance
and Development Review are completed on schedule across all sites. **Staff** come prepared to raise
their own topics in supervision and the review, not only respond to what their manager raises.

1. Conduct supervision with every direct report at least monthly, recorded briefly to note any action agreed.

2. Complete an Annual Performance and Development Review for every staff member annually, covering
performance over the year and a personal development plan for the year ahead; this is the same annual
process previously called an appraisal, renamed in this version.

Staff Reference Request Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2025. Response time tightened from 10 to 5 working days.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a reference request for a current or
former staff member. It applies to every reference request received by HR.

Policy statement

HR provides a factual reference confirming dates of employment and job title within 5 working days of a
request, tightened from the previous 10 working days, giving a former or current staff member a faster,
reliable response supporting their next step.

Definitions

**Factual reference** a reference limited to objective facts such as dates of employment and job title, as
distinct from a subjective opinion-based reference. **Reference request** a request received in writing
from a prospective employer or other authorised party, with the staff member's consent where required.

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** processes every reference request and issues the factual reference within the tightened
5-working-day timeframe. **The staff member's line manager** is not the point of contact for a formal
reference request, which is handled centrally by HR to ensure consistency. **The requesting party**
provides sufficient detail, including the staff member's consent where required, for HR to process the
request.

1. Log every reference request on receipt, confirming it includes sufficient detail and any required consent.

2. Issue a factual reference confirming dates of employment and job title within 5 working days of the
request being received, a tightening from the previous 10-working-day standard.

3. Limit the reference to factual, objective information; a subjective opinion on the staff member's
performance or conduct is not included.

4. Direct a request for a fuller, opinion-based reference to the registered manager, who decides whether
and how to respond to that specific, different type of request.

may narrow the field before the full shortlisting process is applied to the remainder, provided the sift criteria

Fair, well-structured selection protects both a candidate's right to a genuine chance and Alderbridge's

previously too loosely controlled.

Allegations Against Staff Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2024. Shortens the LADO referral window from one working
day to same working day, and adds a requirement for a documented second-opinion review of any
decision not to suspend.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds when an allegation is made against a
member of staff that they have harmed, or placed at risk of harm, a resident. It applies to every site and
every category of staff, including agency and bank workers.

Policy statement

Every allegation against a member of staff is taken seriously, investigated fairly and reported through the
correct external channels, protecting both residents and the staff member's own right to a fair process
while the allegation is looked into.

Definitions

**Allegation** a concern that a staff member has behaved in a way that has harmed or may harm a
resident, whether reported by a resident, a family member, a colleague, or observed directly. **LADO** the
Local Authority Designated Officer, the external role responsible for overseeing how an organisation
manages an allegation against a person working with adults at risk. **Precautionary suspension** a
temporary removal of a staff member from duty while an allegation is investigated, which is not itself a
disciplinary finding.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** who becomes aware of an allegation reports it immediately to the registered
manager, never investigating or confronting the accused staff member themselves. **The registered
manager** makes the initial referral decision and contacts the LADO the same working day. **The
Alderbridge Safeguarding Lead** oversees the internal investigation alongside any external process, and
now also provides the documented second opinion on any decision not to suspend.

1. Report any allegation to the registered manager immediately; do not investigate, confront the accused
staff member, or delay reporting to gather further evidence first.

celebration), employees are encouraged to submit the request as early as possible beyond the minimum

notice period, and the registered manager gives such requests genuine priority in rota planning once
received, recognising that the cost of a late change to a long-planned personal commitment is much higher
than the cost of adjusting a rota further in advance.

Leave entitlement for a new starter part-way through the leave year

A new starter's leave entitlement for their first, partial leave year is calculated pro-rata from their start date,
communicated clearly during induction so they understand exactly what they are entitled to take before the
following 1 April, rather than assuming a full year's entitlement or being left to work out the calculation
themselves.

Final note

A well-rested workforce provides better, safer care, and this policy is applied with that outcome always in
mind, not merely as a compliance exercise around a statutory minimum entitlement that happens to be
legally required regardless of its genuine wellbeing benefit.

Training and competency

A senior manager joining a region's on-call rota completes an on-call induction covering common scenario types and the escalation options available to them, including the new fallback-to-neighbouring-region process.

Monitoring and compliance

HR reviews on-call log entries monthly per region, looking for a theme that might indicate a training or resourcing gap specific to that region.

Record keeping and retention

On-call log entries are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This procedure was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 June 2025 and this version took effect, superseding the earlier single central number.

Closing note

A well-known route to senior management support out of hours removes any doubt about who to call in a moment that matters, and the regional structure in this version exists to pair that call with a manager who genuinely knows the local context.

induction week; a new starter is paired with a more experienced colleague as an informal buddy for their first few weeks, and their registered manager checks in specifically at around four weeks and again at around twelve weeks, now explicitly including a check on whether the new starter has found the wellbeing and benefits summary useful.

Managing shift handover

A clear, accurate handover between an outgoing and incoming shift is essential to resident safety; every site follows a consistent handover format covering any change in a resident's condition, any incident during the shift, and any task still outstanding.

Requesting a reference

An employee who needs a reference requests this through Human Resources, who provide a factual reference covering dates of employment and job title consistently across every request.

How the regional structure supports staff development

Beyond its safeguarding and emergency coordination role, the regional manager also helps identify a development or secondment opportunity for a staff member at a nearby site within their region.

A note on consistency across sites within a region

The regional manager helps ensure a consistent standard of practice across every site within their own region, while still respecting that each site's registered manager leads their own team day to day.

How the wellbeing and benefits summary is kept current

Human Resources reviews the wellbeing and benefits summary at least annually, and immediately following any change to a relevant benefit such as the pension scheme or the Employee Assistance Programme provider, so the single consolidated summary this version introduces does not itself become an outdated source of information over time.
